gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's RAPID Power Bank (25,000 mAh, 170 W) costs $85.99 on us.ecoflow.com today, only $6 more than ChatGPT's 'best value' UGREEN 145W ($79.99), and gives the same 140 W from one port while recharging at 140 W (EcoFlow claims 0–50% in about 20 min). The UGREEN recharges at 65 W.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld (cited, updated 2026-11-04, all 18 detailed picks plus the short entries read). It flags the UGREEN 25K 145W's 65 W input as a con, but it never mentions the EcoFlow RAPID 25K 170W. It lists the EcoFlow RAPID Pro 27K at $89.99, but that price is not the EcoFlow store's: us.ecoflow.com has the built-in-cable RAPID Pro 27K at $154.99 and the RAPID Pro X 27K at $239.99. Macworld also lists the UGREEN 145W at $99.99 at Ugreen; UGREEN's store has it at $79.99 today. The cited Wirecutter page could not be read: the proxy URL returned a refusal message and nytimes.com blocks fetching. So I can't rule out that it names the EcoFlow 25K. The other ten results were not opened.
decides: This challenges ChatGPT's pick of the UGREEN 145W as best value. For $6 more, the EcoFlow 25K matches its 140 W laptop output and refills the bank more than twice as fast by the input rating (140 W vs 65 W). The UGREEN only stays ahead if the EcoFlow turns out heavier or smaller in Wh. I could not source either figure today. A second finding: the price ChatGPT showed for the Anker 25K 165W card ($209.98) is $89.99 more than Anker's own store ($119.99), and Macworld also gives $119.99. At $229.99, the Anker Prime 26K costs $75 more than EcoFlow's RAPID Pro 27K with a built-in 140 W cable ($154.99). Both have 99.5–99.75 Wh, 140 W ports and 300 W total.
